transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-01
Start time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Elena Park (CEO), Marco Li (CTO), Priya Shah (VP Eng), Maya Rivera (Head of Product), Ben Carter (Head of Sales), Aisha Khan (Head of Research), Tom Brooks (Head of Customer Success), Lina Gomez (VP Ops) + ~120 employees (all-hands)

Summary (auto): leadership updates on Q1, roadmap and hiring; brief AMA; security/compliance update.

00:00 Elena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, welcome to our April all-hands, super excited to, uh, kick this off. Quick agenda: Q1 recap, product roadmap, hiring, security update, and AMA.
01:02 Marco Li: Quick note on the numbers — we saw a 22% reduction in p99 latency on v3 runtime for the common prompt sets, um, not perfect but it's moving in the right direction. We also reduced infra cost per token by about 11% thanks to batching and some kernel selection improvements.
02:15 Priya Shah: Yeah and to add, the KV cache changes — sorry the, the K V cash — that we rolled out in mid-March are helping tail latency a lot for chat workloads, especially when sessions reuse prefixes. There are still edge cases with long context where the fallback path spikes. We're looking at smarter cache eviction policies.
03:10 Maya Rivera: On product: Q2 priorities are clear — 1) Dedicated SLA lift, 2) Private deployment polish (VPC onboarding flow), 3) Optimize feature set for caching and quanti-quanization profiles. We'll publish a milestones doc after the meeting.
04:01 Ben Carter: From GTM, renewals look healthy; we had three upsells in March and a couple of PoCs converting to pilots. Main ask from customers is clearer benchmark artifacts for latency and cost, and a certified compliance pack, so please prioritize the SOC2 summary and the audit artifacts.
05:20 Aisha Khan: Research note — our internal evals show the new quantized variants are within 2-3% quality delta on our product prompts, but the noise for red-team prompts is higher, so we want to be cautious. We'll propose a canary/test plan for rollout.
06:45 Lina Gomez: Ops update — ramping up on infra reservations for Dedicated to hit peak season. We're testing burst capacity configs; hope to avoid throttling during high-traffic windows.
07:30 Tom Brooks: Customer success is tracking a couple of enterprise migrations to Private; main blockers are networking (IP allow lists, firewall rules) and KMS integrations. We have a checklist, will share in the CS channel.
08:20 Elena Park: Quick org note — Priya is moving to a larger Eng leadership role owning runtime and infra; congrats. We'll be hiring for two senior infra engineers and a product manager for Private. People ops will post roles today.
09:10 Crowd noise / applause (virtual): woo, congrats, cheers
10:00 Marco Li: Technical deep dive highlights — the kernel selection work got a 15% throughput boost on A100-like runners, and we're seeing better memory compaction with the latest allocator. There was a small regression on peak GPU mmap that we rolled back.
11:15 Priya Shah: We're also tuning continuous batching strategies; some workloads benefit from slightly longer micro-batch windows, but that increases median latency so it's a trade-off. We'll share config knobs for Dedicated customers.
12:40 Audience question (via Q&A): "Any updates on model catalog additions?"
12:55 Maya Rivera: We're onboarding two community models this quarter with Redwood-verified profiles and will publish compatibility notes — including recommended quantization levels and max sequence lengths.
14:05 Audience question: "Private: what's the timeline for on-prem package?"
14:18 Elena Park: Targeting beta for selected customers by end of Q2; full GA depends on a couple compliance gates but we're optimistic.
15:30 Ben Carter: On pricing, we plan to keep tiered usage for Hosted, with reserved pricing for Dedicated and an enterprise license for Private. Nothing final yet, but we'll share proposals with sales leadership next week.
17:05 Aisha Khan: Security/compliance — SOC 2 readiness is on track, control mapping almost done, and we're engaging a third-party auditor. SSO/SAML and audit logs will be in scope. We also have one-off asks around customer-managed keys and HSM integrations; roadmap item for Q3.
19:00 Audience small murmur / side chat: "Will there be region expansions?"
19:12 Elena Park: Yes, Europe expansion is on our roadmap for Q3, APAC region afterwards; partners will help expand capacity sooner.
20:00 AMA open floor — employees asked about promotions, remote policies, and R&D time.
23:30 Employee (Sarah B): How do we prioritize infra debt vs new features?
23:45 Priya Shah: We have a quarterly allocation — 30% runway for infra reliability and performance, 50% for planned roadmap, 20% discovery. That mix may shift.
25:10 Employee (Dev): Any changes to on-call?
25:20 Marco Li: We are evaluating a two-person primary on-call model for runtime but keeping rotation length the same. More details in the infra channel.
27:00 Short break in conversation, music clip shared (virtual)
28:10 Tom Brooks: Customer stories — highlight from a fintech pilot: moving to Dedicated reduced their cost by 18% while meeting latency SLO, they liked the canary rollout feature.
29:40 Ben Carter: Sales ops — we need more benchmark artifacts for different instance types (GPU families), please add a spreadsheet to the shared drive.
31:00 Maya Rivera: Product note — Optimize (the toolkit) will add automated batching suggestions and a new UI for per-route configs; early alpha in May.
33:22 Audience question: "Are we open to community model PRs?"
33:35 Aisha Khan: Yes, we'll accept contributions but they'll go through a vetting/verification pipeline.
35:00 Security question from an employee: "How do we log customer queries for Private?"
35:12 Lina Gomez: For Private deployments, logs can be routed to customer-managed SIEM; by default we keep minimal telemetry necessary for operations, with data residency options.
36:40 Elena Park: Quick financials — revenue growth was positive quarter over quarter, burn is stable, runway extended after Series C; details in the finance deck we'll attach.
38:05 Priya Shah: Tech KR highlight — reduce p99 by another 10% this quarter; major initiative is better KV cache heuristics and a lower-overhead attention kernel.
39:30 Audience: cross talk, "do we have runbooks?"
39:45 Marco Li: Yes, runbooks live in the infra playbook repo; we'll add more examples for Dedicated migrations.
41:00 Open mic: employees shout out team wins, new hires announced.
43:20 Q&A closing
44:00 Elena Park: Recap and next steps — we'll send the roadmap deck, action owners will follow up in the next 72 hours, and we'll schedule a product deep dive demo for partners next week. Thanks everyone.
47:50 Call end

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcribed; a few product names and acronyms may be mis-recognized (KV cache -> K V cash, HSM spelled out/garbled in a couple lines).

References mentioned: "Q2 roadmap deck" (link to internal drive), "performance dashboard" (link to shared Grafana), "SOC 2 control mapping" (confluence link).
